turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's use them. Owen found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that?
I spoke with the vice principal before you came in.
Before I came in isn't the question, Hale. Procedure 4.2 says the parent is called before any mark goes in, and nobody called me. Did the vice principal approve the zero, and when?
She's backing me completely. Policy is policy, and it isn't up to you.
"Policy is policy." Then name the section, because 4.2 says you call me first and 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish a concern. A vice principal backing you isn't evidence. What do you have?
So frankly, this meeting is a courtesy.
"A courtesy." Procedure 4.2 isn't a courtesy, it's a requirement, and the time for it was before the zero went in. Withdraw it, apologise to Owen, or I'm in the principal's office when we're done.
